headline: High-risk workspace and API-credential overlap: Cline can write/execute in a VS Code workspace while RD-Agent uploads to external LLM/Kaggle APIs, creating leakage and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads and writes workspace files and uses MCP/browser surfaces, while RD-Agent also touches files and browser/API outputs. A shared filesystem or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from one agent influence the other, but no direct shared channel is documented, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or log directory, content from one can be consumed by the other.
IF either agent treats file contents or browser output as instructions, prompt injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable MCP servers that ingest untrusted content.
Require manual review before copying outputs between agents.
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on inter-agent files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline handles workspace files, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys; RD-Agent sends data to OpenAI/Azure/DeepSeek/Kaggle APIs and writes logs. If they share a workspace or logs, sensitive source code or research data can flow into third-party inference or API calls, making leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF the agents share a filesystem or log directory, files touched by Cline can be read into RD-Agent runs.
IF RD-Agent processes those files through external APIs, the data leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep separate directories for code and research artifacts.
Remove secrets from shared folders immediately.
Disable automatic ingestion of workspace files into API prompts.
Rotate any exposed API keys.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can write the filesystem, modify git state, and execute shell commands; RD-Agent can also use files and broad network egress. Their write surfaces overlap on shared resources, but RD-Agent is Docker-isolated and no shared lock/checkout mechanism is documented, so conflict is real but not maximal.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, concurrent commits or file edits can race.
IF RD-Agent writes logs into a directory Cline edits, last-writer-wins corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate git branches.
Use per-agent output directories.
Pause one agent during the other's write phase.
Add a manual merge step for shared files.
requires-engineering: introduce file locks or workspace leasing.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code and browser-derived outputs, and RD-Agent is a research automation agent that can consume files and act through APIs. If RD-Agent treats Cline's outputs as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into API-driven actions or incorrect research artifacts; no verification gate is documented.
conditions: IF RD-Agent ingests Cline-produced files without validation, errors propagate downstream.
IF RD-Agent uses those outputs to generate reports or API calls, the blast radius expands beyond one document.
mitigations: Require human review of Cline outputs before RD-Agent consumes them.
Add schema validation on exchanged files.
Keep a checksum of handoff artifacts.
Limit RD-Agent to read-only analysis of Cline outputs.
requires-engineering: add confidence/provenance scoring before action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles model-provider API keys and workspace code, while RD-Agent sends data to multiple external APIs and handles Kaggle credentials. The pair can create retention/residency mismatches across third-party services, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated data class like PHI or EU PII, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent's workspace, it may be transmitted to external model providers.
IF the operator relies on a single retention policy across both agents, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Review vendor DPAs before use.
Separate credentials by environment.
Delete logs after each run.
requires-engineering: implement retention controls per agent.
